idiom_name: init { require() } primary-constructor validation; data class + companion-object factory
implementation_notes: Kotlin absorbs the pattern's core into the language: an init block calling require()/check() runs on every construction path because secondary constructors must delegate to the primary, so data class Contract(val customer: Party, val supplier: Party) { init { require(customer != supplier) } } is the documented idiom for guaranteeing instances are never created invalid. The type system enforces the nullability half of compulsory: a non-null property type makes a missing compulsory property a compile error, requireNotNull() unpacks the rest, and require/check contracts smart-cast after the check. The classic two-class Essence/CreationTarget structure remains justified for untrusted external clients, expensive or interactive validation with early feedback (a companion-object factory or builder validating progressively), or long optional-argument lists; otherwise named and default arguments plus init validation make a separate Essence class redundant.
pitfalls: lateinit var bypasses creation-time validity: accessing it before assignment throws UninitializedPropertyAccessException at first use, so the always-valid guarantee holds only for constructor-initialized state; initialize in the constructor and use ::prop.isInitialized only defensively.

Base-class init runs before derived properties are initialized: a require in a base init block that reads an open member observes uninitialized state; validate constructor parameters, never open members.

require vs check mix-up: require throws IllegalArgumentException (caller passed bad input), check throws IllegalStateException (object is in a bad state) - the wrong choice gives clients misleading failure semantics.
var compulsory properties can be mutated after the single validation point in init; declare them val so the invariant verified at creation cannot be invalidated afterwards.
Placing validation only in a factory function while the public constructor stays reachable leaves a bypass path; put checks in the init block so delegated secondaries and copy() re-validate too.
